key_insight: Across 601 paired perovskite solar-cell simulations, mobile ions had only a small effect on steady-state performance in efficient devices.
engineering_relevance: For device design, ion motion appears less critical than core material and interface parameters such as recombination rate and band offsets, especially in high-performing architectures.
method: Drift-diffusion modeling of perovskite solar cells
Factorial analysis across physically relevant parameter ranges
Paired comparison: each ion-containing device matched to an identical ion-free device
evidence_signal: The study evaluated 1202 total simulated cells arranged as 601 matched pairs spanning n-i-p and p-i-n layouts with organic and inorganic contact layers.
watch_item: The conclusion is based on steady-state simulations, so transient ion effects and real-device degradation may require separate analysis.
paper_title: An Investigation into the Effect of Mobile Ions on the Steady State Performance of Perovskite Solar Cells
